name: Lupin
harvestProduct: grain (protein/energy livestock feed) and/or green manure

evidence.quote: In the summer rainfall regions, where cool and moist conditions prevail, lupines can be planted as soon as the rainy season begins in September/October and when these species are planted under irrigation, they can be planted as early as August
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 17: Lupines, Grain SA (Truter, Dannhauser, Smith & Trytsman), 2019

evidence.quote: ...and in March for winter rainfall regions.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 17: Lupines, Grain SA, 2019
Sweet Lupins - narrow leaf product page, Agricol

evidence.quote: It therefore thrives in the cool, moist areas of the Highveld regions of Mpumalanga, Eastern Free State and the KwaZulu-Natal plateau.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 17: Lupines, Grain SA, 2019

daysToHarvestRange.notes: No SA source gives an explicit day-count from sowing to seed maturity or termination.

evidence.quote: Even though lupin seed is big, it is recommended that the seed should be planted shallow, no more than 3 cm deep.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 17: Lupines, Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: Since white lupin seed is big, high seeding rates (40 kg/ha to 50 kg/ha) are required regardless of row spacing.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 17: Lupines, Grain SA, 2019
Sweet Lupins - narrow leaf (Soet Smalblaar Lupien) product page, Agricol
Bitter Lupins (Bitter Lupiene) product page, Agricol
Narrow Leaf Sweet and Bitter Lupines product page, Barenbrug South Africa

evidence.quote: Lupines are known for their high production of good quality seed and it can be expected under optimal conditions, to yield anything between 1,5 tons/ha to 4 tons/ha depending on prevailing conditions.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 17: Lupines, Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: Atmospheric nitrogen fixation rates of up to 400 kg N/ha has been observed in Europe and Australia.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 17: Lupines, Grain SA, 2019 — figure explicitly attributed to Europe/Australia, NOT South Africa, so not used as an SA N-fixed value.

varieties.name: Lupinus angustifolius (narrow leaf / sweet & bitter types)
varieties.note: Most common species planted in Western Cape, popular for sandy soils. Cultivars: Mandellup, Lila-Baer (sweet); SSL10 (bitter).

evidence.quote: The most common species planted in the Western Cape is mainly L. angustifolius and has become popular for sandy soils
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 17: Lupines, Grain SA, 2019
Sweet Lupins - narrow leaf product page, Agricol

varieties.name: Lupinus albus (sweet white lupin, loamier soils)
varieties.note: Better adapted to loamier soils; thrives in cool moist Highveld areas of Mpumalanga, Eastern Free State and the KZN plateau.

evidence.quote: L. albus is better adapted to the loamier soils. ... It therefore thrives in the cool, moist areas of the Highveld regions of Mpumalanga, Eastern Free State and the KwaZulu-Natal plateau.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 17: Lupines, Grain SA, 2019

zoneNotes.western-cape: Coastal Western Cape is the classic lupin production area, sown March-May, mainly for sheep production.
zoneNotes.highveld: L. albus sweet white lupin, sown September/October (August if irrigated).

gaps: No row/in-row spacing figures found in any source.
The 'up to 400 kg N/ha' N-fixation figure is explicitly for Europe/Australia, not South Africa — no SA-specific N-fixed number was found, so nFixedKgPerHa is left null.
Seed rate varies widely by source/type (40-50kg/ha Grain SA generic vs 50-100kg/ha Agricol/Barenbrug by cultivar) — range reflects this spread rather than one authoritative figure.
summary: Sow windows for both summer-rainfall (Sept/Oct, Aug irrigated) and winter-rainfall (Mar-May) regions, seed rate, sow depth and seed yield (1.5-4 t/ha) are sourced from Grain SA's Part 17 and Agricol/Barenbrug cultivar pages. Row/in-row spacing, days-to-harvest and an SA-specific N-fixation figure are gaps — the only N figure found is explicitly a European/Australian one and was excluded.
